claim: CGEL limits nominal by-obliques to agents and uses that limit in its argument against voice in NPs.
evidence_summary: Bruening’s receipt example makes Gift Processing the recipient of a form. In the advance-knowledge example the investors are the people who knew about the attacks. The latter state can hold without the investors doing anything. Neither by-phrase gives a place, instrument or time.
finding: The examples defeat the agent-only premise in reason (c). Reasons (a) and (b) still stand: nominal forms lack the active/passive contrast, and a single nominal can express both participants as obliques. These data alone do not decide nominal voice.
proposed_wording: The nominal head constrains which participant can be expressed in a by-phrase. Attested possibilities include the agent of a conquest, the recipient in a receipt event, the experiencer of a perception, and the holder of knowledge.
traditional_parallel: Pp. 227–228 separate subject function from typical agenthood. P. 476 uses an agent-only contrast as one argument about nominal voice. Bruening removes that empirical contrast. Showing a double standard would also require holding the competing structural diagnostics constant.
inference: Must the by-phrase of an event or state nominal denote an agent?

evidence.source: Benjamin Bruening (2013). By phrases in passives and nominals. Syntax 16(1), 1–41.
evidence.passage: §16.5.3, p. 476, reason (c) following [57–58]. Of the by-oblique: “In NPs it always has an agentive role”. The immediately following knowledge example is starred. Reasons (a) and (b) concern morphology and the double-oblique pattern.
evidence.example: In (23) an office receives the form. In (25) investors have advance knowledge of attacks. In (21b) the by-phrase also follows the of-phrase, matching the order in CGEL’s starred knowledge example.
evidence.establishes: Recipient and knower are available roles. Reason (c) loses its role contrast. The absence of verbal inflection and the double-oblique pattern remain independent considerations.
